newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr left in an agony of uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr left in an agony of uncertainty.

text.p: The Australian dollar staged a short covering bounce Friday as another day passed with no rate cut, but most felt the fateful event had merely been postponed.

There had been intense speculation the Reserve Bank would end an age of uncertainty and cut this morning, so linking the move to the very favourable inflation and wages data released this week. The policy window passed with no announcement, however, and speculators rushed to cover short positions.
But the dollar remained within the US$0.7310/7440 range held for the last fortnight and dealers doubted it would escape until the rate question was settled one way or the other.
By 5.00 pm (0700 GMT) the dollar had settled at US$0.7402/07 having climbed from an early US$0.7361/66 and US$0.7348/53 late here Thursday.

Resistance had already been felt at US$0.7420 and there was major chart resistance at US$0.7440 and US$0.7475. Equally, support beneath US$0.7330 had impressed so far and analysts expected these to cage the currency while the market waited for the RBA to make up its mind.
Most now reckoned the central bank would move the day after its next board meeting on August 5, meaning the dollar was going nowhere for another week or so.
Many analysts believe the RBA has little choice but to ease given the record low underlying inflation and moderate wages growth reported this week.

It might be reasonably confident growth would pick up to the four percent it wanted without a move, but a cut still looked relatively risk free and the community deserved a reward for such a good inflation performance.

The futures market seemed convinced by the argument with the 90 day bank bill contract for September holding at 94.93, implying a rate of 5.06 percent and so almost fully pricing in a 50 basis point cut in the present 5.50 percent cash rate.

The day's only data were of secondary importance but did provide a rare sign of strength as motor vehicle registrations leapt 13.6 percent in June to a record 62,892. Analysts said the gain was exaggerated by the timing of the budget in early June and the end of the financial year, but would still make a solid contribution to retail sales.
Figures for sale in June and Q2 are due next Thursday but would have to be strong indeed to make the market reconsider its expectations of another cut.
Only if the RBA stayed silent on August 6, would speculation grow that the year-long easing cycle had finally ended.
In the unlikely case this occured, the dollar was certain to rally sharply perhaps back top US$0.7550 or even US$0.7640.
The currency was broadly firmer on the crosses thanks largely to fund flows out of the mark and Swiss franc and into the dollar bloc in general.

The dollar was up at 1.3582/04 marks, which was close to its high for the year, from 1.1433/47 late Thursday and 1.1199/22 francs from 1.0893/08. It also firmed to 86.11/21 yen from 85.10/20, all of which helped to boost it to 57.6 in trade weighted terms from a previous 57.1 close.
